set.body:
Owner request 2026-09-22 ("reference and reconstruction are both important ... we can potentially weight one vs the other; that would be quite valuable").

Goal: an explicit, recorded weight lambda in [0,1] on the structural (order/persistence/fill) component of mapping inference, spanning local reference (lambda=0, bd bd-01M2WVF86T8QEEA1TK8Z0ASJHW) to the named structured reconstruction (lambda=1, bd bd-01M2TAD04SR823TQVG9VPNH6R3). The historical Sherlock preset remains reachable by name; STORYMODEL4S_PRIOR_SCALE-style environment knobs are replaced by this typed parameter.

Acceptance criteria:
1. lambda is part of the versioned inference policy: it changes policy identity and cache keys, is written in every output record, and is refused if out of range or non-finite (fail-closed polarity).
2. lambda=0 reproduces the reference result byte-for-byte and lambda=1 reproduces the reconstruction result byte-for-byte on the WOG miniature and the synthetic multipart case (endpoint parity, mutation-killed).
3. Intermediate lambda is defined mathematically in the ADR 0019 amendment that lands with it (e.g. tempered structural prior / transition strength), with the meaning of the resulting mass stated (model posterior, not calibrated probability).
4. Any lambda>0 output is labelled model-dependent: it is admissible for localization, temporal queries and fMRI projection, and is NOT admissible for organization/order readouts (those require lambda=0 under compatibility bd-01M2WVFV2WGF5BVQHX7JTYYWRH). A test proves an organization request on a lambda>0 result is refused once compatibility lands; until then the facade does not offer organization readouts.
5. The facade CLI exposes lambda (single value or a declared sweep) and the exchange tables carry it as a column.

Out of scope: choosing an optimal lambda (that is benchmark work, post-1.0 research lane).
Evidence: exact SHA, bound test totals/exit, reference-scope gate, separate SD6 cold review.
set.title: [G2] Tunable weight between local reference and structured reconstruction
